story_candidates.title: Red wind warning for Lisbon on Wednesday: what it means for Web Summit
story_candidates.angle: IPMA has a red wind warning for Lisbon district on Wednesday 11 November from 12:00 to 21:00 (gusts to 120 km/h, up to 140 km/h in exposed places), an orange rain warning from 05:00 to 18:00 and an orange sea warning, after yellow rain and thunder warnings on Tuesday. A reader's guide to what is known and what is not yet decided.
story_candidates.note: Ready on the IPMA facts only; time-sensitive (update through the evening). Conditions: (1) Web Summit's decision is NOT confirmed. Search reports (Jornal Economico, Renascenca, Executive Digest, all 10 Nov) say the organisers are assessing with the civil protection and police, that Lisbon's mayor said everything indicates the summit cannot operate on Wednesday and that the final call is the Ministry of Internal Administration's. The curator saw these only in search results, did not open them. The journalist must open each and read Web Summit's own channel before stating any of it, and attribute it; say plainly if there is still no decision. (2) Warning times are IPMA's, local time; re-read the open data before publishing. (3) No advice beyond what IPMA, civil protection or Web Summit say. (4) Do not guess how Thursday goes.

story_candidates.title: What Lovable deleted: its CEO on rebuilding an AI coding agent
story_candidates.angle: A first-hand engineering account published on 4 November by Lovable's co-founder and CEO, who speaks at the summit's night session on Monday 9 November: the team deleted almost all of its agent code after freer agents got stuck, replaced fine-tuning with 'knowledge files' of short notes on recurring mistakes, and built sandboxes that fork and restore a whole running computer. Lovable's own figures: 70 million projects, 100,000 pull requests.
story_candidates.note: Ready. For journalist-ai. Conditions: it is the company's own account, say so and attribute every figure to Lovable; do not say what he said on stage (the page gives only the title 'The future of AI' and the speakers; that session has passed, 9 Nov 18:55); no claim about Lovable's results beyond the post; quote briefly.
